lem-rpm-curved-charge-action-variation:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure, as required for the metric-selected Levi–Civita connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $O\subseteq M$ be open and let $A$ be a $C^2$ covector field on $O$; define the $C^1$ two-form $F=dA$ by $F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a$ in each chart. Fix constants $c>0$, $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$. Let $z:[a,b]\to O$ be a $C^2$ future-directed timelike curve, where $a<b$ are proper-time values in seconds and $U=dz/d\tau$ satisfies $g(U,U)=-c^2$. For every $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variation $z_\epsilon$ through timelike curves in $O$, with variation field $J=\partial_\epsilon z_\epsilon|_{\epsilon=0}$ and $J(a)=J(b)=0$, define

$$S[z_\epsilon]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(\partial_\tau z_\epsilon,\partial_\tau z_\epsilon)}\,d\tau+q\int_a^b A(\partial_\tau z_\epsilon)\,d\tau.$$

Then the first variation is

$$\delta S=\int_a^b\left[-m\,g(J,\nabla_UU)+qF(J,U)\right]d\tau.$$

Consequently, $z$ is stationary under all local chart-supported fixed-endpoint variations if and only if

$$m(\nabla_UU)_a=qF_{ab}U^b,$$

equivalently $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$, where $F^\sharp(v)$ is defined by $g(F^\sharp(v),w)=F(w,v)$. The statement is local to a potential domain; no global potential is assumed.
lem-rpm-external-charge-local-ivp:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for its canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure, so the metric-selected Levi–Civita connection $\nabla$ exists by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $O\subseteq M$ be open and let $F$ be a $C^1$ alternating covariant two-tensor field on $O$ (a two-form); define $F^\sharp$ by $g(F^\sharp(v),w)=F(w,v)$. Fix $m,c>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, an event $x_0\in O$, and $U_0\in T_{x_0}M$ with $g(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$ future directed. Then the initial-value problem

$$\dot x=U,\qquad \nabla_UU=(q/m)F^\sharp(U),\qquad (x(\tau_0),U(\tau_0))=(x_0,U_0)$$

has a unique local $C^2$ solution on an open proper-time interval containing $\tau_0$. Any two solutions with these initial data agree on every connected part of their common domain containing $\tau_0$. Along the solution, $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ remains future directed. The result is local; it asserts no completeness or global existence for arbitrary external fields.
lem-rpm-charge-gauge-boundary:
## Statement

Let $O$ be a potential domain with a $C^2$ metric $g$, a $C^2$ one-form $A$, and $F=dA$. Let $\chi\in C^3(O,\mathbb R)$ and set $A^\chi:=A+d\chi$. For $a<b$, any $C^2$ future-timelike curve segment $z:[a,b]\to O$ parameterized by proper time $\tau$ so $g(z',z')=-c^2$ for $c>0$, constants $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$, and the functional

$$S_A[z]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(z',z') }\,d\tau+q\int_a^b A(z')\,d\tau,$$

the field strength is unchanged, $dA^\chi=dA$, and

$$S_{A^\chi}[z]-S_A[z]=q\bigl(\chi(z(b))-\chi(z(a))\bigr).$$

Thus the difference is constant over every fixed-endpoint variation, so stationarity and the kinetic covector $p:=mU^\flat$ are gauge invariant. If the local covector $\pi_A:=p+qA$ is defined, then $\pi_{A^\chi}=\pi_A+q\,d\chi$. These are local statements on $O$; they assert no global exactness of $F$.

def-rpm-charge-spin-model.physical_scope: Definitions of one classical massive charged and spinning test body on a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian background: constant positive mass and fixed charge/gyromagnetic parameter, proper-time worldline, kinetic momentum, orthogonal polarization and magnetic-moment convention, and prescribed external two-form with local potential. These are ideal model quantities and SI conventions, not a field equation, motion law, measured gyromagnetic value or quantum-spin construction. Self-gravity, self-field evaluation, radiation reaction, collisions, electric dipole forces, field-gradient translational forces and higher multipoles are excluded as stated in the Definition.

def-rpm-charge-spin-model:
## Definition

Use the smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian background $(M,g,N)$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the distinct chart, observer, congruence, tetrad and worldline meanings of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. The metric and time orientation are prescribed data, not dynamical variables. A **charged spinning test body** in this definition consists of the following model quantities along a massive worldline $z:I\to M$:

- $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open interval whose parameter is proper time $\tau$ in seconds; $z$ is $C^2$, future-directed and timelike, and $U:=dz/d\tau$ obeys $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The SI conversion constant is $c>0$ metres per second; in a flat specialization use the affine Minkowski model and the proper-time decomposition of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]].
- The constant rest-mass parameter $m>0$ has unit kilogram, and the constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ has unit coulomb. They are primitive model parameters; this definition does not derive them from the background field or from another framework.
- The **kinetic four-momentum** is the derived vector $P:=mU$ along $z$, with unit kilogram metre per second. It is distinct from the potential-dependent covector defined in [[lem-rpm-charge-gauge-boundary]].
- The **spin or polarization vector** is a $C^1$ tangent vector field $s(\tau)\in T_{z(\tau)}M$ constrained by $g(s,U)=0$, so it lies in the positive-definite instantaneous rest space $U^\perp$. Its unit is angular momentum, kilogram metre squared per second. This is a classical model vector; no quantization or quantum spin state is defined here.
- The gyromagnetic ratio $g_s\in\mathbb R$ is a dimensionless primitive species parameter. In the instantaneous rest space the model defines the magnetic-moment vector by $\mu=(g_s q/2m)s$, with unit ampere metre squared. No value $g_s=2$ is assumed, and this constitutive relation is not deduced from Lorentz covariance or classical electromagnetism.
- The prescribed external electromagnetic field is a $C^1$ alternating covariant two-tensor $F$ on an open region of $M$, independent of the unknown curve. Define $F^\sharp:T M\to T M$ by $g(F^\sharp(v),w)=F(w,v)$. In the flat specialization, a named inertial chart with $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres uses $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, matching [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]. On the curved background, $F$ is only a two-form; at an event its components in a chosen orthonormal tetrad use the same algebraic convention. Such a tetrad is a basis field, not a coordinate chart or an observer congruence, as distinguished in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. The components in an orthonormal tetrad have tesla units. This is an explicit curved-background model input. The cited EM supplier is a flat Minkowski definition and does not derive a curved field or curved Maxwell system.
- On any open potential domain where a $C^2$ covector field $A$ exists, $F=dA$ with components $F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a$ and $A$ has tesla metre components in the stated coordinates. No global potential is assumed, and no Maxwell equation or constitutive law is imposed here.

This is a test-body model on a fixed background: self-gravity, gravitational backreaction, self-field evaluation, radiation reaction, collisions, electric dipole moments, field-gradient translational forces and higher multipoles are outside this definition. Units follow the framework-local SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and do not identify quantities across frameworks.

post-rpm-external-charge-action.physical_scope: Adopted dynamics for one massive charged test body on a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian background, on finite timelike curve segments contained in a local potential domain. The background metric and external electromagnetic two-form are fixed; the model excludes self-field evaluation, self-gravity, radiation reaction, variable mass or charge, and any global-potential or global-solution claim.

post-rpm-external-charge-action:
## Postulate

Adopt the following motion principle for the massive charged test body of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]]. On any finite segment $z:[a,b]\to O$ in a local potential domain, with $z$ a $C^2$ future-timelike curve and fixed endpoints, the physical trajectories of this idealized model are the stationary points of

$$S[z]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(z',z') }\,d\lambda+q\int_a^b A(z')\,d\lambda,$$

where $\lambda$ is an orientation-preserving curve parameter (use seconds for SI evaluation), $A$ is the prescribed $C^2$ external potential, $F=dA$, $m>0$ is constant rest mass, $q$ is constant charge, and $c$ is the SI conversion constant. With $\lambda=\tau$ in seconds, coordinates in metres and $A$ in tesla metres, $S$ has units joule seconds. The potential and metric are fixed inputs, independent of the particle path. This is a local action postulate: no global potential is assumed, and a global field equation or global trajectory is not part of the postulate. Its Euler–Lagrange consequence is proved separately in [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]].

This model describes a test body: it does not evaluate the body's own field, include self-gravity, or adopt radiation reaction, variable mass or charge, electric dipole forces, or spin-dependent translational forces. The postulate is an adopted model assumption, not a deduction from the electromagnetic field equations or a claim that nature follows this action.

post-rpm-bmt-dipole-model.physical_scope: An adopted classical polarization transport law for a charged massive test body in a prescribed external field, with Lorentz-force translation. The curved-spacetime form is an independent model extension; it is not inferred from the flat homogeneous-field BMT paper, from covariance alone or from experiments. No quantum-spin ontology or measured value of the gyromagnetic ratio is asserted.

post-rpm-bmt-dipole-model:
## Postulate

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected Levi–Civita connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $U$ and the prescribed external two-form $F$ be as in [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], and let the translational motion obey the adopted action law [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]]. For a $C^1$ spin or polarization vector $s$ along the worldline with $g(s,U)=0$, define $G:=g_s/2$ and $K:=F(s,U)=g(s,F^\sharp(U))$. Adopt the transport law

$$\nabla_U s=\frac{q}{m}\left[G F^\sharp(s)-(G-1)\frac{U}{c^2}K\right].$$

This is an ideal classical external-field dipole model with constant $q,m,g_s$. Its flat homogeneous-field specialization is the BMT polarization law in the stated RPM convention. The formula on a curved background, and its use for a spatially varying prescribed field, are separately adopted model assumptions; neither follows from the flat BMT source or from general covariance alone.

The model excludes an electric dipole moment, field-gradient or Stern–Gerlach translational forces, spin backreaction, radiation reaction, collisions and higher multipoles. The parameter $g_s$ is not fixed to $2$ and no measured value is asserted. Using this classical vector to represent a real quantum particle's polarization is a correspondence assumption; the postulate does not construct quantum spin or claim empirical validation.

pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivale.physical_scope: A conditional equivalence for finite fixed-endpoint timelike curve variations in a local potential domain of the prescribed curved background model: stationarity of the adopted external charged-particle action is equivalent to the covariant Lorentz-force equation with the RPM SI sign convention. It asserts no global potential, local or global trajectory existence, self-field, radiation reaction, or empirical claim.

pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivale:
## Statement

Assume the charged test-body quantities and local potential domain of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], the flat-space sign convention of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and the adopted fixed-endpoint action postulate [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]], and assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure. For a finite $C^2$ future-timelike curve segment $z:[a,b]\to O$ in that domain, where $a<b$ are proper-time endpoints, and the local $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variations of the postulate, choose the orientation-preserving parameter $\lambda=\tau$; the segment is stationary for the adopted action if and only if

$$m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U),\qquad (\nabla_UU)_a=\frac qm F_{ab}U^b.$$

This is a model deduction: it establishes the equation equivalent to stationarity of the postulated functional, not the physical truth of the postulate.

pthm-rpm-charge-mass-shell.physical_scope: Local solutions of the external-field charged test-body model with constant $m>0$ and $q$ preserve the future timelike four-velocity shell in a fixed curved Lorentzian background. The laboratory three-force and power identities are asserted only in the flat Minkowski specialization with a named inertial SI chart and the compatible EM tensor convention. No global completeness, self-force, radiation reaction, measurement or empirical claim is included.

pthm-rpm-charge-mass-shell:
## Statement

Assume the charged test-body quantities of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], the field convention of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and the stationary-action equivalence [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]], and assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure. For every future-timelike initial datum $(x_0,U_0)$ with $g(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$, the equation of motion has a unique local solution by [[lem-rpm-external-charge-local-ivp]]. Along it the kinetic four-momentum $P=mU$ remains future timelike and satisfies

$$g(P,P)=-m^2c^2.$$

In the flat Minkowski specialization, use the massive-particle momentum result [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] under its stated model assumptions, and choose a named inertial chart with $x^0=ct$, $E,B$ defined by [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and $\mathbf v$ the Euclidean spatial chart velocity. Set $\gamma:=(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Then, with $\mathbf p=m\gamma\mathbf v$ and $E_{\rm part}=\gamma mc^2$ supplied by [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]], the same equation gives

$$\frac{d\mathbf p}{dt}=q(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B),\qquad \frac{dE_{\rm part}}{dt}=q\,\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf v.$$

The mass-shell and force statements are conditional deductions within the specified model; they do not establish empirical applicability.

ex-rpm-pure-gauge-free-charge.physical_scope: Symbolic flat-Minkowski example of the adopted external-field massive charged test-body action, on finite fixed-endpoint timelike segments and under the inherited countable-choice hypothesis. The pure-gauge potential changes a local canonical covector without changing the kinetic momentum or producing a Lorentz force. No self-field, radiation reaction, measured energy, empirical finding or interaction mechanism is asserted.
